response.sql: WITH total AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM `order`), per_account AS (SELECT a.account_id, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_cnt, COUNT(o.order_id) * 1.0 / (SELECT n FROM total) AS share FROM account a LEFT JOIN `order` o ON o.account_id = a.account_id GROUP BY a.account_id), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_s FROM per_account), above AS (SELECT p.account_id, p.order_cnt, p.share FROM per_account p WHERE p.share > (SELECT avg_s FROM avg_share)) SELECT SUM(order_cnt) AS total_orders, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - (SELECT avg_s FROM avg_share)) AS avg_excess_share FROM above;

assumptions.assumption: The total number of orders is COUNT(*) over the `order` table, and every order's account_id matches an account row (enforced by the foreign key), so the per-account counts sum to this total.
The average share is the unweighted mean of the per-account shares over all accounts in `account`, including accounts with zero orders.
'Above the average' means strictly greater than the average share.
'On average how far their share is above the average share' is the mean of (share minus the overall average share) across the selected accounts, unrounded.
